summary.text: The early modern period, roughly 1500 to 1800, is a historical period defined mainly by the history of Europe and the broader concept of modernity.
It has no exact start or end date, and events such as the Fall of Constantinople in 1453 or the start of the Reformation have been proposed as its start.
Recent historians argue its most important worldwide feature was the spread of globalization, alongside the rise of mercantilism and the Scientific Revolution.

items.prompt: One textbook starts the early modern period with the Fall of Constantinople, another with the Reformation. Why do both exist?

options.label: One of them is simply a mistake
There is no exact starting date, and several events have been proposed
Constantinople and the Reformation happened in the same year
The period began separately in each country

items.explain: No exact date marks the beginning, and various events have been proposed as its start.

items.prompt: Why did the idea of an early modern era first arise in the study of Europe?

options.label: Europe was the only continent with written records
Historians in Asia rejected the idea outright
Europe was the first to use firearms
Europeans had long divided their history into ancient, medieval and modern

items.explain: The concept grew out of European history, which had traditionally been divided into ancient, medieval and modern periods.

items.prompt: A historian studying the whole world, not just Europe, names one defining feature of 1500 to 1800. Which fits recent scholars' view?

options.label: The spread of globalization
The retreat of trade between regions
The end of all monarchies
The decline of mercantilism

items.explain: Historians in recent decades have argued that, worldwide, the most important feature was the spread of globalization.

items.prompt: Newly sustained contact between the Americas and the rest of the world greatly altered the human environment. What is this exchange called?

options.label: The Commercial Revolution
The Great Divergence
The Columbian Exchange
The Age of Revolutions

items.explain: The Columbian Exchange linked the Old World and the New World and greatly altered the human environment.

items.prompt: Firearms helped the Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal empires expand. What else did their strength rest on?

options.label: Staying small and cut off from rivals
Centralized states, efficient bureaucracies and tax collection
Ruling only one religious group of people
Giving up trade routes and tax income

items.explain: Their strength also rested on centralized states, efficient bureaucracies, tax collection, control over trade routes and administration of diverse societies.

items.prompt: The early modern period gave way to the late modern period in the late 18th century. What marked the change?

options.label: The start of the Renaissance and the printing revolution
The Fall of Constantinople and the Age of Discovery
The Columbian contact and the Reformation
The Industrial Revolution and the American and French Revolutions

items.explain: The transition was marked by the Industrial Revolution, the American Revolution and the French Revolution.
